section_summary: The section finishes a British report on Japan’s economic recovery and prospects for British merchandise trade, shipping, banking, insurance, and investment. State Department memoranda then consider whether Japanese aid should come under the Economic Cooperation Administration and how to handle economic deconcentration. The remaining material concerns Hokkaido’s economy, labor disputes, Communist activity, and fears of Soviet expansion; several related enclosures have been withdrawn, and the final memorandum continues beyond page 431.

subfiles.title: Japanese economic recovery and opportunities for British trade
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s economic prospects and future opportunities for British trade and investment.
subfiles.summary: The report expects Japan to depend on imported food and raw materials while rebuilding export industries, tourism, and transport. It anticipates limited direct merchandise trade with the United Kingdom but stronger prospects for British shipping, banking, insurance, accounting, and possibly investment. Its closing pages compare prewar trade with likely postwar conditions and stress uncertainty about coal, industrial limits, reparations, and the size of Japan’s merchant fleet.

subfiles.title: Possible Inclusion of Japan Within the Orbit of ECA Operations
subfiles.about: Reports William Y. Elliott’s question about placing Japanese aid under ECA alongside Korean aid.
subfiles.summary: Butterworth urges NA to assess the proposal before Congress raises it.

subfiles.title: Status of FEC 230 on Japanese economic deconcentration
subfiles.about: Proposes withdrawing U.S. support for an outdated Far Eastern Commission deconcentration proposal.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman requests Kennan’s views on a drafted statement and its timing.

subfiles.title: Possible Inclusion of Japan within the Orbit of ECA Operations
subfiles.about: Comments on an internal proposal to consider transferring the Japanese aid program to ECA.
subfiles.summary: Allison supports discussion but urges careful departmental review before consultations with Army, SCAP, or ECA.

subfiles.title: Clearance of Attached Letter Relating to FEC-230
subfiles.about: Questions a proposed request for detailed information about Japan’s Deconcentration Review Board.
subfiles.summary: Fearey argues that existing information is adequate and that a broad inquiry could unsettle deconcentration progress or intrude on SCAP’s implementation duties. He recommends narrowing any request and affirming support for recent SCAP actions.

subfiles.title: Comments on memorandum concerning the Japanese recovery program
subfiles.about: Critiques proposed arguments for presenting Japanese recovery policy to the 81st Congress.
subfiles.summary: The writer cautions against judging Japan’s antitrust laws by U.S. statutes, given Japan’s different economic structure. The memorandum also calls for broader stock ownership and safeguards so foreign investment does not reinforce monopolies or provoke resentment.

subfiles.title: Routing note on Tokyo despatch No. 742
subfiles.about: Directs Butterworth to a summary of Tokyo despatch No. 742.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the bulky enclosures remain in NA.

subfiles.title: Attached Tokyo’s 742
subfiles.about: Summarizes Lawrence’s Hokkaido report for possible circulation within FE.
subfiles.summary: Green highlights territorial friction with the Soviets, fears of U.S. withdrawal, Communist organizing, labor law disputes, police weaknesses, and economic obstacles. He notes Lawrence’s proposal for a U.S. consulate in Hokkaido.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal notice for Tokyo despatch enclosure
subfiles.about: Records the removal of a restricted enclosure associated with Tokyo despatch No. 742.
subfiles.summary: A National Archives notice marks the enclosure as access restricted.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal notice for sub-enclosure No. 1
subfiles.about: Records the removal of sub-enclosure No. 1 to Tokyo despatch No. 742.
subfiles.summary: A National Archives notice marks the sub-enclosure as access restricted.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal notice for sub-enclosure No. 2
subfiles.about: Records the removal of another enclosure related to Tokyo despatch No. 742.
subfiles.summary: A National Archives notice marks the enclosure as access restricted.

subfiles.title: Observations During an Orientation Trip to Hokkaido Concerning Current Political and Economic Conditions
subfiles.about: Transmits Lawrence’s report on political and economic conditions observed during a Hokkaido visit.
subfiles.summary: The despatch summarizes Soviet border tensions, Communist activity, labor disputes, police capacity, and obstacles to Hokkaido’s industrial growth. It proposes steps to reassure residents of U.S. interest, including a consular presence, and describes the industrial and statistical reports attached to Lawrence’s memorandum.

subfiles.title: Observations Made as a Result of a Visit to Hokkaido
subfiles.doc_type: Enclosed memorandum with table of contents
subfiles.about: Reports interviews and observations from a September 1948 visit to Hokkaido.
subfiles.summary: The table of contents outlines sections on Communism, labor, economic production, education, the Occupation, and a peace treaty. The surviving opening pages describe Hokkaido’s distinct conditions, fears of Soviet expansion, disputes over nearby islands, Communist recruitment, and the effects of the Showa Denko scandal. They then examine opposition to Ordinance No. 201 and the proposed National Public Service Law revision, particularly demands to retain collective bargaining for government workers. The memorandum continues after page 431.
